native/insert-text-controlled.description: Every text input is CONTROLLED_TEXT_INSERTION_COMMAND. JS lets the browser insert most typed characters into the DOM and syncs the model from the input event; the native views never edit their own text (Q40). The resulting state is the same.

native/replacement-keeps-caret.description: A replacement before a collapsed caret (autocorrection, a spelling fix, Writing Tools) leaves the caret where it was, shifted by the replacement's change in length, as NSTextView and UITextView do. JS leaves the caret after the replaced text unless the key that accepted it follows ($maybeMoveSelectionPastTrailingAcceptanceBoundary).

native/delete-content-forward.description: deleteContentForward dispatches DELETE_CHARACTER_COMMAND(false). JS dispatches DELETE_LINE_COMMAND(false) over the browser's one-character target range, which removes the same character.

native/composition-in-model.description: IME marked text is written through the model with insertText on the composing node from COMPOSITION_START_COMMAND to COMPOSITION_END_COMMAND; JS lets the browser compose in the DOM and reads the text back. No COMPOSITION_START_CHAR placeholder is inserted (desktop WebKit inserts none either).

native/select-all-menu.description: Select All from the menu or the iOS edit menu dispatches SELECT_ALL_COMMAND, as Command-A does. In a browser the menu item selects natively and only a selectionchange follows.

native/ios-hardware-tab.description: On iOS, a hardware Tab that no KEY_TAB_COMMAND handler prevents reaches UITextView, which inserts a tab character. Safari moves the focus out of the contenteditable. On macOS, insertTab: moves the focus as a browser does.

native/rtf-paste.description: A pasteboard with RTF and no HTML (copied from a native app) is converted to HTML before PASTE_COMMAND, as Safari converts it when a page reads such a pasteboard.

native/lexical-pasteboard-type.description: application/x-lexical-editor travels on the pasteboard as the type dev.lexical.editor. Safari keeps a page's custom MIME types in WebKit's private pasteboard data, so Lexical JSON copied in a browser reaches the native views as HTML and text, and the reverse.

native/drag-move-between-editors.description: A drag moved into another editor is removed from the source by the source view when its drag session ends as a move (deleteByDrag there), where JS has the drop side find the source editor's root in the shared DOM.

native/caret-format-at-run-boundary.description: A location on the boundary of two text nodes is a point at the end of the node before it, and a caret there takes that node's format, as Cocoa's typing attributes come from the preceding character. WebKit keeps its DOM caret in the node an arrow key moved through, so after moving left onto a boundary JS has the point at the start of the node after it (which $normalizeSelectionPointsForBoundaries keeps when a range starts there) and a caret with that node's format.
scenarios: TextEntry > Can insert a paragraph between two text nodes (rich)
TextFormatting > Can select multiple text parts and format them with shortcuts (rich)

native/vertical-move-by-x-position.description: ArrowUp and ArrowDown keep the caret's horizontal position in points, so where it lands depends on the fonts' metrics, which differ between WebKit and TextKit. The Linux scenario replay has no layout and keeps the character column, so the caret can land a character away from WebKit's.
scenarios: TextFormatting > Can insert range of formatted text and select part and replace with character (rich)

native/drag-selection-forward.description: A selection made by dragging, tapping, clicking or a program is forward in the model, since a native view's selected range has no direction; only a shift-arrow (a shifted key the text view handles) extends backward from the model's anchor. WebKit makes a right-to-left drag a backward selection.

native/word-move-from-range.description: With a range selected, Option-Left and Option-Right move a word from the range's edge, as NSTextView's moveWordLeft: and moveWordRight: and UITextView's Option-arrows do (verified on macOS 27 with NSTextView and LexicalNSTextView, and on the iOS 27 simulator with LexicalUITextView: with 15..<17 selected in "  123 abc 456  def  ", left lands at 10 and right at 18). WebKit first collapses the range to its edge and stops there when the edge is a word boundary (15 and 17).
scenarios: Navigation > native navigation > can navigate through the formatted text word by word (rich)

native/ios-format-toolbar-in-edit-menu.description: On iOS the playground's floating text format toolbar (FloatingTextFormatToolbarPlugin) is not a popup: its bold, italic, underline and strikethrough join the system edit menu that UIKit shows above a selection, with the rest of its buttons in a Format submenu, so the two do not cover each other. The web playground shows the popup above the selection on wide viewports and leaves it out below 1025 pixels (isSmallWidthViewport). On macOS it is the web's popup.

native/image-resizer-inside-the-image.description: The playground's ImageResizer handles are drawn just inside the image's edges, not 6 pixels outside them as the web's .image-resizer CSS places them, because the image's hosting view is the size of the image and neither AppKit nor UIKit hit-tests a point outside it. While a handle is dragged the image draws at its new size only where it shrinks, since the text view keeps the attachment at its old size until the handle is let go, when the node takes the size (the web restyles the on every pointermove).

native/ios-code-action-menu-at-selection.description: On iOS the playground's code action menu (CodeActionMenuPlugin: the block's language and the copy button at its top right) is shown while the selection is in a code block, since a touch screen has no hover. The web playground and macOS show it while the mouse is over a code block. Prettier's button is not ported on either platform.

native/block-decorator-drag.description: The playground moves any selected block decorator (a page break, a horizontal rule) by dragging it, the way ImagesExtension moves an image (DecoratorDragExtension), where the web playground drags only images: a native decorator's view needs a drag to move it, while on the web the other block decorators are moved with the draggable block handle. On iOS a selected decorator lifts on a long press, which UIKit's drag interaction requires, where the web drags it on pointer movement.

native/draggable-block-macos-only.description: The playground's DraggableBlockPlugin (the + and grip handle at a block's left, drag to reorder, the drop line) is ported on macOS only, where it shows while the window is wider than 1025 points, as the web shows it above a 1025px viewport. iOS does not have it: the web hides it on narrow screens, a touch has no hover to show the handle, and a long press on text is UIKit's own text drag, loupe and selection, which a handle beside every block would fight. Its + button adds a paragraph with the '/' component picker open in it, where the web opens a copy of the picker with a filter field beside the handle.

native/embeds-in-web-views.description: The playground's YouTube, X and Figma embeds draw their iframe (and, for a tweet, Twitter's widgets.js) in a WKWebView inside the embed block, loaded from a page at https://playground.lexical.dev/ so that YouTube's player accepts the embedding origin. A tweet's widget sets its own height, which the page reports so the block grows to it; until then the block is 200 points tall with "Loading...". On iOS the web view does not scroll on its own, and a click or tap on the video goes to the player, as an iframe takes its own clicks; the rest of the line selects the block. The menu that offers to embed a pasted link is the default node menu (Dismiss, Embed), drawn at the link as the typeahead menus are.

native/tree-sitter-code-tokens.description: The playground highlights code with LexicalCodeTreeSitter, not Prism, so a block's CodeHighlightNodes split and are typed as the grammar's highlights query captures them, mapped to Prism's token names (prismTokenType): the text is the same, the token boundaries and highlightType values can differ. In ``console.log(`Hello, ${who}!`)``, Prism leaves `console` and `${who}` untyped and types the backticks as punctuation, where tree-sitter types `console` as builtin, the backticks and `who` as string and `${` and `}` as punctuation; tree-sitter also types numbers and booleans as constant in some grammars (Rust, JSON) and builtin types as builtin. Only the ten bundled grammars highlight (JS, TS, Swift, Python, JSON, HTML, CSS, Rust, Go, shell); the picker's C, C++, Java, Markdown, Objective-C, PowerShell, SQL and XML stay plain until their grammars are added. No conformance vector depends on Prism's tokens: serialization/code builds its highlight nodes by hand.

native/poll-and-sticky-note.description: The playground's PollNode and StickyNode are the web's (the same JSON and HTML), drawn natively. A poll is 400 points wide, as .PollNode__container's min-width, and 320 on an iPhone, whose editor is narrower; a vote is cast as one of upstream's animal names, picked at launch, as useCollaborationContext's name is without collaboration. A sticky note is drawn over the text view at its offset from the text's top left corner, as upstream portals it to the document's body at the root element's rect, and scrolls with the text: on macOS it is in the text view, on iOS in the window over the text view and clipped to it, since the text view's gestures take its subviews' touches. Its handwriting face is the system's Noteworthy, for the Reenie Beanie web font, and a SwiftUI drag gesture in the note keeps its buttons from firing, so its drag is a pan of the note's own on iOS and an AppKit view behind the note's content on macOS; its buttons are tap gestures on iOS, where a hosted Button does not fire, and plain Buttons on macOS, where a tap gesture does not. The Insert menu has Sticky Note and the '/' menu does not, as on the web.

native/equations-katex-in-web-views.description: The playground's EquationNode is the web's (the same JSON, and HTML byte for byte with KaTeX's markup), with KaTeX 0.16.27 bundled in the app rather than a native math renderer, so equations look and parse exactly as on the web. Each equation draws in a small WKWebView sized to what KaTeX reports, and exportDOM runs the same katex.min.js in JavaScriptCore over a minimal DOM that serializes as Chromium does. The double-click editor is a native text field between grey $ (or $$) markers, and the Insert Equation dialog is a native form with an Inline toggle in place of a checkbox.

native/context-menu-system-items.description: The playground's ContextMenuPlugin adds Remove Link, Copy as Markdown, Paste as Plain Text and Delete Node before the system's own menu items: the macOS context menu and, on iOS, the edit menu after the selection's formats. The web draws a custom menu, only with its shouldUseLexicalContextMenu setting (off by default), that also has its own Cut, Copy and Paste; native always adds its items, which leave the browser's or system's menu in place, and leaves Cut, Copy and Paste to the system's items. On iOS, where the edit menu belongs to the selection rather than a click, Remove Link and Delete Node act on the selection's anchor node instead of the node under the pointer.

native/emoji-glyphs-and-caption-mentions.description: The playground's EmojiNode and EmojisExtension are the web's (the same JSON and HTML), in the document and in an image's caption, but the views draw the emoji's own character rather than the web's 16px image behind transparent text (.emoji.happysmile and the others in index.css), since TextKit has no background image for a run of text. The caption's mentions menu inserts a MentionNode: upstream's CaptionEditorExtension shows the menu (MentionsPlugin) but registers only EmojiNode, so choosing a mention there throws that MentionNode is not configured; the Swift caption registers it.
